coverage_gaps: The Layer 1B input visible to this call was partially truncated; the merged universe therefore emphasizes the visible grid/electrical node and uses hypotheses for several other nodes.

Need live primary-source verification for every hypothesis using SEC filings, company annual reports, earnings transcripts, investor presentations, FERC/NRC/DOE records, utility IRPs, ISO interconnection queues and project announcements.
Need current market-cap, valuation, short-interest, analyst-coverage and earnings-revision checks before deciding whether names are truly underfollowed or already consensus.
Need non-US expansion: Europe, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Canada and selected emerging-market grid/nuclear/power suppliers are underrepresented.
Need transformer-specific public-company mapping beyond Eaton/GE Vernova/Powell; private suppliers and diversified subsidiaries may hide the true bottleneck.
Need nuclear-component and nuclear-fuel-cycle verification beyond Centrus/Cameco/BWXT, including qualified suppliers, conversion, fabrication, transport and licensing services.
Need gas-turbine supply-chain detail, including hot-gas-path components, controls, repair services, compressors, fuel infrastructure and long-lead parts.
Need data-center cooling breakdown into liquid cooling, chillers, rear-door heat exchangers, immersion, water infrastructure, fire protection, controls and electrical/mechanical contractors.
Need regional utility mapping for PJM, ERCOT, SPP, MISO, WECC and Southeast load growth to separate regulated rate-base beneficiaries from merchant power-price beneficiaries.

Need falsification triggers for each node: lead-time normalization, backlog cancellation, customer insourcing, capacity additions, tariff/commodity pressure, policy reversal, financing stress and hyperscaler capex digestion.

memory_update.text: Layer 1C ranking suggests the clearest Energy and Power Chain chokepoint cluster is electrical hardware plus execution: switchgear, substations, busway, electrical balance-of-system, qualified contractors, testing and commissioning.
Powell, Eaton, Hubbell and PLPC form a useful grid/electrical-hardware validation set, with Eaton/Hubbell as references and Powell/PLPC as more Serenity-style underfollowed or niche exposures.
MYR Group and IES Holdings should be tracked as execution-layer candidates because qualified electrical labor, procurement, substation construction and commissioning may be independent bottlenecks.

Nuclear should remain decomposed into fuel cycle, HALEU, uranium, qualified components, licensing and EPC; SMR developers should be treated as speculative shadow candidates until project evidence improves.
Layer 2 should verify market caps, revenue exposure, backlog, valuation, analyst coverage and source filings for all underfollowed candidates before narrowing the universe.
The current universe is still US-heavy and should be expanded with Canada, Europe, Japan, Korea and Taiwan suppliers in transformers, grid components, nuclear services, cooling and power electronics.

Several candidates were kept as hypotheses despite incomplete evidence because the Serenity method allows weak-evidence names into Layer 1 when they have explicit hidden signals and falsification paths.

summary: Layer 1C merged and deduplicated the Energy and Power Chain initial universe using the Serenity funnel: start from power-demand growth, map physical chokepoints, separate reference leaders from underfollowed suppliers, and rank for later evidence validation. The highest-priority cluster is grid/data-center electrical hardware and execution, followed by nuclear fuel/components, dispatchable generation, thermal/cooling, storage/inverters, and regulated power assets. This is a research-priority universe only, not a trading recommendation.
universe_method: multi-step: theme decomposition -> node expansion -> dedupe/rank
